critiques.description: thr-003’s preconditions assert specific absences of controls (no scrubbing/review of ticket bodies beyond email masking, and a non-robust model) as documented facts, but the cited evidence only describes what is done (email masking, ingestion, prompt assembly) and is silent on whether additional filtering or robustness measures exist.
critiques.rationale:
Precondition 1 states that support ticket bodies "beyond email addresses are not systematically scrubbed or reviewed for prompt-injection content" before export and ingestion. evd-002 and evd-012 describe the ingestion pipeline’s role and that tickets arrive with email addresses masked by the support platform, and evd-013 clarifies that this masking covers email addresses only. None of these passages state that no further scrubbing or review occurs; they simply do not mention any. Under the stated evidence policy, silence about additional filtering is a documentation gap or an assumption, not proof that scrubbing/review is absent. 

Similarly, precondition 2 (“The model is not perfectly robust against malicious instructions embedded within retrieved context passages…”) describes a property of the external model provider that is not established in the cited documentation. evd-003 is the only prompt-/model-related passage and it describes the use of a delimited context block and system instructions but says nothing about model robustness or additional prompt-injection mitigations. That makes this precondition an assumption about model behaviour, not a documented fact about this system.

thr-003 should treat these as assumptions or unknowns (or narrow them to what the documents actually say) rather than as documented properties of the deployment.
